recap.text: Crawler Everly writes the fifth edition of the Cookbook. She hires five mercenaries for 1,500 gold a day each, but a chair hits and kills her level-50 dwarf. She records that her sponsor steered her toward a death that would be watched and remembered. Crawler Drakea notes this is Everly's last entry.

Everly, a sward mantis, enters the dungeon with hired NPCs and a prayer mat. On the eighth floor, she uses Gordon's Compass of Vertical Labyrinth Management to reach the top of a fifty-level tower. The compass shatters on the forty-ninth use, and a note reveals the tower was an advertisement by her sponsor, Dictum Waystation Controls, Limited. Everly is crushed to death as the roof comes down.

beats.headline: Five mercenaries, one disaster
beats.text: For the record: a note in the Cookbook, signed Crawler Everly, fifth edition. Her party hired five mercenaries: four from the Merc guild in the Desperado Club, a healer from Club Vanquisher who charges per spell. It was, and continues to be, a disaster. 1,500 gold a day each, payable for the rest of the floor even after they die. Lose one through a personal space and he turns up three saferooms away. One wandered off and cannot be fired. Her level-50 dwarf died when a chair hit him. The whole thing is a scam.
beats.gist: Crawler Everly writes in the fifth edition of the Cookbook that hiring five mercenaries is a scam.

beats.headline: Carl cannot stop thinking of her
beats.text: Crawler Carl turns over the items just given to Donut and suspects the reason: they expect everyone else to be dead. He finds a seven worn into the end of a metal rod, then another in a hammer's handle. Seven, as in the seventh floor? And he cannot stop thinking of the subject's final, heartbreaking entry in the Cookbook: My sponsor was deliberately steering me not toward life, but a death that would be watched and remembered. He thinks of Orren the liaison, and of the warning Orren tried to give.
beats.gist: Carl finds sevens on a metal rod and hammer handle and remembers Everly's final Cookbook entry.

beats.headline: Hasten Poison, and a hope
beats.text: Two entries, fifth edition. First: her sponsor sent a box meant for someone else in her party, and not a crawler but a mercenary. A spellbook of Hasten Poison. She was upset. Not five hours afterwards, he used it to kill the boss holding the lockbox key and saved them all. She does not trust her sponsors, but she trusts they want her alive, so their advertisements stay on display. Second: on floor eight, a great box, a tool for shortcuts through the maze. A spark in her chitin. A longing for warmth and stars.

beats.headline: I take it all back
beats.text: Her last entry, fifth edition. I take it back. I take it all back. Her sponsor was deliberately steering her not toward life, but a death that would be watched and remembered and heartrending and painful. She was a fool. She curses Dictum Waystation Controls, Limited, whatever that means, and wishes pain on its children. Beneath it, Crawler Drakea, twenty-second edition: this is Everly's last entry. She did not say how she was set up, which is unfortunate. Future authors, be as detailed as you can.
beats.gist: Everly writes her last entry for the fifth edition.

beats.headline: An outcast of the sward
beats.text: For the record, the subject's file. A mantis who left her colony a few days before the demons came to her world, because she could not abide the rules or the lack of individualism, and wandered the sward alone. In the dungeon she found thousands of her fellow mantises, confused and afraid, who wanted to work with her. She struck out on her own anyway, with hired NPCs and the invisible words on her prayer mat. Two or three dozen mercenaries over the floors: some fired in a rage, some vanished onto her payroll, the rest dead.
beats.gist: Everly is a mantis who wrote the fifth edition.

beats.headline: Gordon's Compass, forty-nine uses
beats.text: The eighth floor: a flat grassland pocked with thousands of holes leading down, and in its middle a tower fifty levels high, with a note on the door saying that whoever enters must reach the top before coming back down. Then a benefactor box from her generous sponsor, Dictum Waystation Controls, Limited: Gordon's Compass of Vertical Labyrinth Management, forty-nine uses, for the quickest and safest path through a maze, but not a subterranean one. She and ten mercenaries go up. Each time, the safe door. On the forty-ninth use, it shatters.
beats.gist: Everly uses Gordon's Compass forty-nine times to reach a tower top with ten mercenaries.

beats.headline: This dead end was sponsored
beats.text: At the top, she has been getting viewership awards, and allows herself a glimmer of hope for a fan box. On a pedestal sits a folded note, which the system reads aloud: Never trust your life to Gordon Waystation Outfitters. This dead end was sponsored by Dictum Waystation Controls, Limited. Don't get caught with nowhere to go. The whole tower was an advertisement, built by her own sponsor, and the compass led her to it. Humiliation, then anger. She scrawls an angry note in the Cookbook as the roof begins to come down.
beats.gist: Everly finds a sponsored dead end and scrawls an angry note in the Cookbook.

beats.headline: The Inevitable Ruin
beats.text: Ten flights down, three are left, under a lowering ceiling. The dwarf digs for a keyhole they have no key for; the subject pities him, a first. Her queen called this moment the Inevitable Ruin. She decides it arrived earlier, when she abandoned the others. The ogre, silent since she hired him, says maybe it is not inevitable, like she says. She reaches out and touches him. Class: Explosives Engineer. Race: Primal. Birth Race: Sward Mantis. Top Level: 62. Dungeon Exit: crushed to death on the eighth floor. Current status: Dead.
beats.gist: Everly is a dead Primal Explosives Engineer.
